<div class="page-shell">

<header class="masthead">
  <div class="eyebrow">WebR practical</div>
  <h1>Reading check_model() with the SUNSHINE checklist</h1>
  <p>The <code>check_model()</code> function draws every regression diagnostic at once — which can feel like a wall of plots. The <strong>SUNSHINE</strong> checklist gives you eight things to look for, so you always know what each panel is for.</p>
</header>

<div class="callout warning">
<strong>Heads up — first run is slow.</strong> The first time you run a cell, your browser downloads the R packages (<code>performance</code>, <code>see</code>, <code>ggplot2</code>, and friends) and compiles the plots. This can take <strong>30–90 seconds</strong>. After that it is fast. If a cell looks stuck, give it a moment before re-running.
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>The SUNSHINE checklist</h2>

Whenever you fit a linear regression, the same eight assumptions decide whether the results can be trusted. They spell **SUNSHINE**:

<div class="sun-grid">
  <div class="sun-card think"><div class="sun-letter">S</div><div class="sun-label">Sample size</div><div class="sun-tag">Think</div></div>
  <div class="sun-card think"><div class="sun-letter">U</div><div class="sun-label">Uncorrelated errors</div><div class="sun-tag">Think</div></div>
  <div class="sun-card plot"><div class="sun-letter">N</div><div class="sun-label">No multicollinearity</div><div class="sun-tag">Plot</div></div>
  <div class="sun-card plot"><div class="sun-letter">S</div><div class="sun-label">Shape (linearity)</div><div class="sun-tag">Plot</div></div>
  <div class="sun-card plot"><div class="sun-letter">H</div><div class="sun-label">Homogeneity of variance</div><div class="sun-tag">Plot</div></div>
  <div class="sun-card plot"><div class="sun-letter">I</div><div class="sun-label">Influential points</div><div class="sun-tag">Plot</div></div>
  <div class="sun-card plot"><div class="sun-letter">N</div><div class="sun-label">Normality of residuals</div><div class="sun-tag">Plot</div></div>
  <div class="sun-card think"><div class="sun-letter">E</div><div class="sun-label">Exogeneity</div><div class="sun-tag">Think</div></div>
</div>

<div class="legend">
  <span><span class="swatch" style="background:#5fbfbf"></span> <strong>Plot</strong> — <code>check_model()</code> draws a panel you can read directly.</span>
  <span><span class="swatch" style="background:#f5c542"></span> <strong>Think</strong> — a design / reasoning question no plot can settle.</span>
</div>

<p style="margin-top:1rem">The key insight: <code>check_model()</code> handles the <strong>five "Plot" letters</strong> for you. The other three — <strong>S</strong>ample size, <strong>U</strong>ncorrelated errors, and <strong>E</strong>xogeneity — are about your study design and data collection, so you have to reason about them yourself.</p>

After answering all questions, <strong>your completion code will be revealed.</strong> Enter it into the LMS to mark this practical complete.

</section>

  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="a">The steps for cleaning a dataset.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="b">The arguments of the <code>lm()</code> function.</label>

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 2</div>
  <p>Three SUNSHINE letters are marked <strong>"Think"</strong> rather than <strong>"Plot"</strong>. Why?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="a">They are less important than the others.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="b">They depend on study design and data collection, so no diagnostic plot can settle them.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="c">R has not implemented them yet.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. The 'Think' letters are not unimportant — they just can't be judged from a plot, because they depend on design and how the data were collected."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>From model to checklist in two lines</h2>

The workflow is the same as always: fit a model, then hand it to `check_model()`.

```r
library(performance)

model <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)

check_model(model)
```

As the panel appears, walk the **five "Plot" letters** of SUNSHINE in order. Each one tells you exactly which panel to look at and what "good" looks like:

<table class="summary-table">
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Letter</th><th>Panel to read</th><th>Good sign</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td><strong>N</strong> — No multicollinearity</td><td>Collinearity bars (VIF)</td><td>Bars stay low / in the green zone (needs 2+ predictors).</td></tr>
    <tr><td><strong>S</strong> — Shape (linearity)</td><td>Residuals vs fitted</td><td>Green line stays roughly flat.</td></tr>
    <tr><td><strong>H</strong> — Homogeneity</td><td>Scale–location spread</td><td>Green line roughly flat (constant spread).</td></tr>
    <tr><td><strong>I</strong> — Influential points</td><td>Residuals vs leverage</td><td>No point sitting far outside the dashed contour.</td></tr>
    <tr><td><strong>N</strong> — Normality</td><td>Q-Q style plot</td><td>Dots hug the reference line / stay in the band.</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

</section>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">

  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="a">Five of them.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="b">All eight.</label>

The other three are 'Think' letters."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Worked example: fuel economy of cars</h2>

We will use `mtcars`, a built-in dataset of 32 cars, and model fuel economy (`mpg`) from each car's **weight** (`wt`) and **horsepower** (`hp`). Run the cell to fit the model.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>Step 1: fit the model</h3>

```{webr-r}
library(performance)

model <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)

summary(model)
```

</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>See the regression itself</h2>

Before walking the SUNSHINE letters, it helps to *look* at the model. The cell below plots fuel economy against weight and draws the fitted straight line — the line whose assumptions the rest of the checklist interrogates.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>The fitted regression line</h3>

```{webr-r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
plot(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars,
     pch = 19, col = "#00565e",
     xlab = "Weight (1000 lbs)", ylab = "Miles per gallon",
     main = "Fuel economy vs weight, with fitted line")
abline(lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars), col = "#f5c542", lwd = 3)
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 4</div>
  <p>The model has 32 cars and two predictors. Which SUNSHINE letter does that fact speak to most directly — and is it something a plot can verify?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="a"><strong>H</strong> (homogeneity), and yes a plot verifies it.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="b"><strong>S</strong> (sample size), and no — it is a "Think" letter you judge yourself.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="c"><strong>E</strong> (exogeneity), and yes a plot verifies it.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. The number of observations relative to predictors is the Sample-size letter, and you judge it by thinking, not from a residual plot." data-incorrect="Not quite. 'How many observations do I have for this many predictors?' is the Sample-size (S) letter — a 'Think' letter, not something a plot settles."></div>
</div>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>Step 2: draw the full SUNSHINE panel</h3>

```{webr-r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 13
check_model(model)
```

</div>

<div class="callout try">
Walk the panel using the five Plot letters: <strong>N</strong>o multicollinearity, <strong>S</strong>hape, <strong>H</strong>omogeneity, <strong>I</strong>nfluential points, <strong>N</strong>ormality. Compare each panel's dots against its green reference line or band.
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Match each letter to its panel</h2>

Match each of the five "Plot" SUNSHINE letters to the panel it points you to, then check your answers.

<div id="arg-match">
<table class="summary-table">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Panel description</th>
      <th>SUNSHINE letter (pick from dropdown)</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Bars (one per predictor) showing how inflated each coefficient's variance is; should stay low.</td>
      <td>
        <select class="arg-select" data-answer="N1">
          <option value="">Select one</option>
          <option value="N1">N — No multicollinearity</option>
          <option value="S">S — Shape (linearity)</option>
          <option value="H">H — Homogeneity</option>
          <option value="I">I — Influential points</option>
          <option value="N2">N — Normality</option>
        </select>
      </td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Residuals vs fitted values; a flat green line means a straight line fits.</td>
      <td>
        <select class="arg-select" data-answer="S">
          <option value="">--</option>
          <option value="N1">N — No multicollinearity</option>
          <option value="S">S — Shape (linearity)</option>
          <option value="H">H — Homogeneity</option>
          <option value="I">I — Influential points</option>
          <option value="N2">N — Normality</option>
        </select>
      </td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Spread of residuals across fitted values; a flat line means the noise is the same size everywhere.</td>
      <td>
        <select class="arg-select" data-answer="H">
          <option value="">--</option>
          <option value="N1">N — No multicollinearity</option>
          <option value="S">S — Shape (linearity)</option>
          <option value="H">H — Homogeneity</option>
          <option value="I">I — Influential points</option>
          <option value="N2">N — Normality</option>
        </select>
      </td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Leverage vs residual size; flags a single point that may be dragging the line.</td>
      <td>
        <select class="arg-select" data-answer="I">
          <option value="">--</option>
          <option value="N1">N — No multicollinearity</option>
          <option value="S">S — Shape (linearity)</option>
          <option value="H">H — Homogeneity</option>
          <option value="I">I — Influential points</option>
          <option value="N2">N — Normality</option>
        </select>
      </td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Q-Q style plot comparing residuals to a bell curve; dots should follow the reference line.</td>
      <td>
        <select class="arg-select" data-answer="N2">
          <option value="">--</option>
          <option value="N1">N — No multicollinearity</option>
          <option value="S">S — Shape (linearity)</option>
          <option value="H">H — Homogeneity</option>
          <option value="I">I — Influential points</option>
          <option value="N2">N — Normality</option>
        </select>
      </td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<button type="button" class="match-button" id="arg-match-check">Check matches</button>
<div class="match-feedback" id="arg-match-feedback"></div>
</div>

</section>

Replace each `____` with the right piece, then run the cell.

<script>
const COMPLETION_CODE = "SUNSHINE";
const COMPLETION_REQUIRED = 7;

function shuffleArgSelectOptions() {
  document.querySelectorAll("#arg-match .arg-select").forEach((sel) => {
    const options = Array.from(sel.options);
    const placeholder = options.shift();
    options.sort(() => Math.random() - 0.5);
    sel.replaceChildren(placeholder, ...options);
    sel.selectedIndex = 0;
  });
}

document.getElementById("arg-match-check")?.addEventListener("click", () => {
  const selects = document.querySelectorAll("#arg-match .arg-select");
  const feedback = document.getElementById("arg-match-feedback");
  let allSelected = true;
  let allCorrect = true;

  selects.forEach((sel) => {
    sel.classList.remove("correct-choice", "incorrect-choice");
    if (!sel.value) {
      allSelected = false;
      sel.classList.add("incorrect-choice");
      return;
    }
    if (sel.value === sel.dataset.answer) {
      sel.classList.add("correct-choice");
    } else {
      allCorrect = false;
      sel.classList.add("incorrect-choice");
    }
  });

  feedback.classList.remove("is-correct", "is-incorrect");
  if (!allSelected) {
    feedback.classList.add("is-incorrect");
    feedback.textContent = "Choose a letter for every row, then check again.";
  } else if (allCorrect) {
    feedback.classList.add("is-correct");
    feedback.textContent = "All five matches are correct.";
  } else {
    feedback.classList.add("is-incorrect");
    feedback.textContent = "Not quite. Check the rows highlighted in red and try again.";
  }
});

shuffleArgSelectOptions();

function updateCompletion() {
  const cards = document.querySelectorAll(".practice");
  const correct = document.querySelectorAll(".practice.is-correct").length;
  const total = cards.length;
  const progress = document.getElementById("code-progress");
  const box = document.getElementById("code-box");
  const value = document.getElementById("code-value");

  if (progress) {
    progress.textContent = correct + " of " + total + " correct (need at least " + COMPLETION_REQUIRED + ")";
  }

  if (box && value) {
    if (correct >= COMPLETION_REQUIRED) {
      value.textContent = COMPLETION_CODE;
      box.style.display = "block";
    } else {
      box.style.display = "none";
    }
  }
}

document.querySelectorAll(".practice").forEach((card) => {
  const button = card.querySelector("button");
  const feedback = card.querySelector(".practice-feedback");
  const answer = card.dataset.answer;

  button.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const selected = card.querySelector("input[type='radio']:checked");
    card.classList.remove("is-correct", "is-incorrect");
    card.querySelectorAll("label").forEach((label) => {
      label.classList.remove("correct-choice", "incorrect-choice");
    });

    if (!selected) {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      feedback.textContent = "Choose an answer first, then check it.";
      updateCompletion();
      return;
    }

    const selectedLabel = selected.closest("label");
    const correctInput = card.querySelector(`input[value="${answer}"]`);
    const correctLabel = correctInput ? correctInput.closest("label") : null;

    if (selected.value === answer) {
      card.classList.add("is-correct");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.correct;
    } else {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("incorrect-choice");
      if (correctLabel) correctLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.incorrect;
    }

    updateCompletion();
  });
});

updateCompletion();
</script>
